summary: Jörg B. Quenzer is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He held a post at the University of Hamburg and served on the editorial board of Studies in Manuscript Cultures, both attested in 2016.

Jörg Heimbel works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tibet University and completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg by 2014 under Dorji Wangchuk and Franz-Karl Ehrhard. By 2019, he was a Tibetan lecturer at Hamburg.
Jörg Plassen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He has served as a professor at Geumgang University and at Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2013).

Jørn Borup specialized in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Aarhus University (~1998–2002) under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader, and later served there as associate professor from around 2008 to 2023.

Jürgen Hanneder is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Marburg (~1993–1996) under Michael Hahn. He worked at Halle (~1999–2007) and became a professor at the University of Marburg in 2007.
Jürgen Neuß is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied under Harry Falk and completed his PhD at the Free University of Berlin in 2007.

Jürgen Renn works in history/archaeology and philosophy. After earning his PhD from TU Berlin in 1987, he held posts at Boston University, became Director at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (1994), and MPI of Geoanthropology (2022).

K. A. Nilakanta Sastri was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at the University of Madras (~1909–1913). He later served there as Professor of Indian History and Archaeology (~1929–1946) and at Mysore (~1952–1956).

K. A. Subramania Iyer specialized in Indology, linguistics, and philosophy, studying at the University of London and University of Paris. He was Professor and Head of Sanskrit at the University of Lucknow (1921–1960) and later Vice-Chancellor at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University.
K. Ammini Amma was an Indology scholar who conducted research as a student at the University of Madras, attested in 1940 and 1971.
K. Balasubramania Iyer was an Indologist. He served as secretary at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 1945) and as managing editor of the Journal of Oriental Research, Madras.
K. Kanapathypillai was an Indologist and linguist. He was educated at Hartley College and studied at the University of London from around 1936 to 1940.

K. Kunjunni Raja was an Indologist and linguist who completed doctorates at the University of Madras (1948) and the University of London (1954). He served as Professor and Head of the Sanskrit Department at the University of Madras starting in 1951.

K. L. Dhammajoti specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Kelaniya and served in leadership roles at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (~1990–2003) and the University of Hong Kong (~2004–2014).

K. Madhava Krishna Sarma was an Indologist who studied under C. Kunhan Raja. He was associated with the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1940, 1971) and served as curator of the Anup Sanskrit Library (attested 1946).

K. Meenakshi is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She completed her PhD under M. A. Mehendale at Savitribai Phule Pune University by 1964 and held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 1983).

K. Munirathnam is a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology who studied under N. S. Ramachandra Murthy. He served as Director (Epigraphy) I/c at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 2013–2018).

K. N. Jayatilleke was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Ludwig Wittgenstein at the University of Cambridge (1945–1948). He served as Senior Lecturer in Philosophy at the University of Ceylon (~1950–1963).

K. Sambasiva Sastri was an Indologist. Succeeding T. Ganapati Sastri, he served as curator at the Oriental Manuscripts Library, University of Kerala, and the Oriental Research Institute and Manuscripts Library from around 1928 to 1937.
K. Srinivasan is an Indologist who served as a professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College (attested 2008) and was associated with the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2020).
